title: Improve checkpoint discoverability for agents
summary: Architecture analysis for making the egg-checkpoint CLI discoverable by downstream agents (Tester, Documenter, Integrator) through targeted prompt injection and agent mode command updates. The recommended approach is prompt-only changes (Option A from the refine analysis): add role-specific checkpoint hints to orchestrator prompts, agent mode commands, and mission.md. No schema changes, new tooling, or new CLI wrappers needed. The existing checkpoint.md rule (62 lines, already loaded) provides the CLI reference; the gap is telling agents when and why to use it.

problem_statement.description: The egg-checkpoint CLI captures rich cross-agent context (transcripts, tool calls, files touched, token usage), but agents rarely use it. The CLI works, documentation exists (docs/guides/checkpoint-access.md, 220+ lines), and a Claude Code rule is loaded (sandbox/.claude/rules/checkpoint.md, 63 lines). But nothing in agent prompts, mode commands, or handoff data tells agents to use checkpoints. Agents only discover them by accident.
goals: Make downstream agents (Tester, Documenter, Integrator) aware of checkpoints as a context source
Add role-specific checkpoint hints to orchestrator-generated prompts (highest leverage)
Update agent mode commands with checkpoint workflows per role
Add checkpoint to mission.md context sources table
Add error-recovery hints (egg-checkpoint list --status failed) for revision cycles
Keep changes minimal — prompt text only, no schema migrations or new tooling

checkpoint_infrastructure.location: sandbox/.claude/rules/checkpoint.md (63 lines), docs/guides/checkpoint-access.md (220+ lines), bin/egg-checkpoint CLI
checkpoint_infrastructure.mechanism: egg-checkpoint CLI queries checkpoints stored on egg/checkpoints/v2 branch. Supports list, show, browse, context, cost commands with multi-dimensional filtering (issue, pipeline, agent-type, phase, status). The checkpoint.md rule is loaded into every agent session via Claude Code rules system.
checkpoint_infrastructure.gap: The rule provides HOW to use checkpoints but nothing tells agents WHEN or WHY. No orchestrator prompt, agent mode command, or mission rule mentions checkpoints.

approaches.name: Prompt-only changes (recommended)
approaches.description: Add role-specific checkpoint hints to orchestrator prompts (_build_role_context, _build_agent_prompt, _build_phase_scoped_prompt), agent mode commands (tester, integrator, documenter), and mission.md. No schema changes, no new tooling, no new CLI. The existing checkpoint.md rule provides CLI reference; these changes tell agents when and why to use it.
pros: Highest leverage: orchestrator prompts reach every agent session automatically
Lowest risk: only text changes to prompt templates and markdown files
No schema migrations or backward-compatibility concerns
No new maintenance burden — leverages existing checkpoint.md rule for CLI reference
Approved by both refine reviewers (agent-design and refine)
Covers items 1-4 from the issue (agent mode commands, mission.md, orchestrator prompts, error recovery hints)
cons: No structured checkpoint linking (agents query by pipeline/issue, not exact ID)
Slightly increases prompt token usage per session (~5-10 lines per role)
Does not cover items 5-8 from the issue (slash command, handoff enrichment, revision summaries, egg-agent-context wrapper)

approaches.name: Prompt changes + handoff data enrichment
approaches.description: Everything in Option A, plus extend AgentOutput to include checkpoint_ids field so downstream agents receive exact checkpoint IDs in EGG_HANDOFF_DATA. Wire up the existing AgentExecutionModel.checkpoint_id field (already in the schema but never populated).
pros: Agents get exact checkpoint IDs without querying
Builds on existing schema support (AgentExecutionModel.checkpoint_id already defined)
cons: Requires knowing checkpoint ID at session completion time — depends on checkpoint write timing
Schema change to AgentOutput class in orchestrator/handoffs.py
More moving parts to debug if checkpoint IDs are missing or stale
Checkpoint writes may be asynchronous (gateway-managed), creating race conditions

approaches.name: Full suite — prompts + handoff data + new tooling
approaches.description: Everything in Options A and B, plus create egg-agent-context convenience wrapper CLI and /checkpoint-discovery slash command.
cons: Highest implementation cost and maintenance burden
egg-agent-context is redundant with egg-checkpoint context
Slash command only useful when manually invoked — agents in pipeline mode don't invoke slash commands
Over-engineering: the core problem is lack of prompting, not lack of tooling

recommended_approach.name: Prompt-only changes
justification: The refine analysis recommended Option A and both reviewers (agent-design and refine) approved with no feedback requiring changes. The agent-design reviewer specifically noted this approach 'orients agents toward existing checkpoint tooling without pre-fetching, rigid procedures, or over-engineering'.

The core problem is discoverability, not tooling. The checkpoint CLI works. The checkpoint.md rule is already loaded. Agents just need to know WHEN and WHY to use checkpoints. Adding 5-10 lines of role-specific hints to orchestrator prompts and 3-5 lines to each mode command solves this.

The orchestrator prompt injection (_build_role_context, _build_agent_prompt) is the highest-leverage change because it reaches every downstream agent session automatically — no opt-in required, no docs to read first.

Deferring handoff enrichment (Option B) is correct because: (a) checkpoint write timing may be asynchronous, creating race conditions with ID capture; (b) the existing AgentExecutionModel.checkpoint_id field can be wired up as a separate follow-up once checkpoint write ordering is understood; (c) agents can query by pipeline/issue which is reliable and sufficient.
The egg-agent-context wrapper (Option C) would duplicate egg-checkpoint context. The slash command is low-value since pipeline agents don't invoke slash commands.

technical_decisions.decision: Inject checkpoint hints into orchestrator prompts (not just mode commands)
technical_decisions.rationale: The orchestrator prompts (_build_agent_prompt, _build_role_context) are generated server-side and injected into every agent session automatically. Mode commands require the agent to invoke a slash command. Orchestrator injection is guaranteed to reach agents; mode commands are supplementary.
alternatives_considered: Mode commands only — rejected: agents may not invoke them, especially in pipeline mode
Modify checkpoint.md rule only — rejected: rule is already loaded but agents don't know when to use it

technical_decisions.decision: Use brief nudge + role-specific one-liner (not full workflow blocks) in orchestrator prompts
technical_decisions.rationale: The checkpoint.md rule (62 lines) is already loaded into every session with full CLI reference and common workflows. The orchestrator hint only needs to tell agents WHEN to use checkpoints and provide the specific command for their role. A 1-2 line hint per role adds ~5-10 lines total to the prompt. Full workflow blocks would duplicate the rule.
alternatives_considered: Single generic line for all roles — rejected: less actionable, agents may not know which command to run
Full 5-10 line workflow per role — rejected: duplicates checkpoint.md rule content, wastes tokens

technical_decisions.decision: Add checkpoint hints to all execution role cycles, not just revision cycles
technical_decisions.rationale: Even on first-cycle runs, downstream agents (tester, documenter, integrator) benefit from checkpoint context. In Tier 2/3 pipelines, there are checkpoints from the coder's session (and potentially from analysis/plan phases). Limiting hints to revision cycles would miss the primary use case: tester reviewing coder's work.
alternatives_considered: Revision cycles only — rejected: misses the primary handoff discovery use case
Conditional based on checkpoint availability — rejected: over-engineering, agents can handle 'no checkpoints found' gracefully

technical_decisions.decision: Add error-recovery hint to both orchestrator revision prompt and revision checklist
technical_decisions.rationale: The _build_phase_scoped_prompt revision checklist (line 2785-2794) is the natural place for 'check prior failed sessions'. Adding it there ensures coders in revision cycles see it. The _build_agent_prompt revision feedback section (line 2454-2457) covers tester/documenter revision cycles. Both are needed.
alternatives_considered: Orchestrator only — rejected: doesn't cover phase-scoped prompt revision checklist
Mode commands only — rejected: less reliable than server-injected hints

technical_decisions.decision: Defer handoff enrichment (checkpoint_ids in AgentOutput) to a follow-up issue
technical_decisions.rationale: The AgentExecutionModel.checkpoint_id field already exists in the contract schema (models.py:361-365) but is never populated. Wiring it up requires understanding checkpoint write timing — checkpoints may be written asynchronously by the gateway after agent exit. This creates a race condition: the orchestrator may try to capture checkpoint_id before the checkpoint is written. Solving this correctly is a separate concern from prompt discoverability.
alternatives_considered: Wire up checkpoint_id now — rejected: checkpoint write timing uncertainty makes this unreliable without additional investigation
Poll for checkpoint ID with retry — rejected: adds complexity to orchestrator agent lifecycle management

technical_decisions.decision: Do not create egg-agent-context wrapper or /checkpoint-discovery slash command
technical_decisions.rationale: egg-agent-context would duplicate egg-checkpoint context --pipeline $EGG_PIPELINE_ID. The slash command is low-value because agents in pipeline mode don't invoke slash commands (they receive orchestrator-generated prompts). Both add maintenance burden without proportional value.
alternatives_considered: Create both — rejected: over-engineering per refine analysis and agent-design reviewer feedback
Create slash command only — rejected: pipeline agents don't use slash commands

technical_decisions.decision: Include coder-mode.md in scope with a revision-cycle-only hint
technical_decisions.rationale: The coder is typically the first agent with no prior checkpoints. But in revision cycles, checking prior failed sessions (egg-checkpoint list --status failed) helps coders understand what went wrong. In Tier 3 multi-phase execution, a Phase 2 coder could benefit from Phase 1's checkpoint. A conditional hint ('if this is a revision cycle...') adds value without noise on first cycles.
alternatives_considered: Exclude coder-mode.md entirely — rejected: misses revision-cycle value
Unconditional hint — rejected: noise for first-cycle coders with no prior checkpoints

risks.description: Prompt token increase may affect agent performance on context-heavy sessions
risks.mitigation: Keep hints to 1-2 lines per role in orchestrator prompts. Total addition: ~10-15 lines across all roles. checkpoint.md rule (62 lines) is already loaded — incremental cost is minimal. Mode command additions are ~3-5 lines each.

risks.description: Agents may over-rely on checkpoints and spend tokens on unnecessary checkpoint queries
risks.mitigation: Hints are phrased as optional context gathering, not mandatory steps. The checkpoint.md rule already says 'common workflows' — agents will self-regulate based on relevance.

risks.description: Checkpoint queries may fail or return empty results (no checkpoints yet)
risks.mitigation: Agents handle 'no results' gracefully — an empty list is not an error. First-cycle agents in new pipelines will see no checkpoints and move on. No special error handling needed.

risks.description: Changes to orchestrator prompt functions may conflict with other in-flight PRs
risks.mitigation: Changes are additive (appending lines to existing lists). No structural changes to function signatures or control flow. Git merge should handle line-level additions cleanly.

constraints: Changes are prompt-text-only — no Python logic changes, no schema migrations
Orchestrator prompt additions must be concise (1-2 lines per role) to minimize token impact
Mode command additions should follow existing section structure (## headings, numbered steps)
All checkpoint commands must use existing environment variables ($EGG_PIPELINE_ID, $EGG_ISSUE_NUMBER)
No new dependencies, CLIs, or slash commands
Backward-compatible: agents without checkpoint data simply see no results from queries
Do not modify the checkpoint.md rule's core CLI reference — only optionally add a 'When to Use' preamble

Q1_coder_mode_hints.question: Should coder-mode.md also get checkpoint hints?
Q1_coder_mode_hints.resolution: Yes, but only for revision cycles. Add a conditional hint: 'If this is a revision cycle, check prior failed sessions.' The coder is typically first with no prior checkpoints, but revision cycles and Tier 3 multi-phase execution benefit from checkpoint awareness.

Q2_orchestrator_hint_specificity.question: How specific should orchestrator prompt hints be?
Q2_orchestrator_hint_specificity.resolution: Role-specific one-liners (option b from the analysis). A brief nudge referencing the checkpoint rule plus the specific command for each role. Not a full workflow block (duplicates checkpoint.md) and not a generic single line (not actionable enough).

Q3_all_cycles_or_revision_only.question: Should we add checkpoint hints to revision-cycle prompts only, or all cycles?
Q3_all_cycles_or_revision_only.resolution: All cycles for execution roles (tester, documenter, integrator). They always benefit from checkpoint context — even first-cycle testers want to see the coder's session. Error-recovery hints (--status failed) only in revision cycles.

Q4_error_recovery_location.question: Should the error-recovery hint be in the orchestrator prompt or the agent mode command?
Q4_error_recovery_location.resolution: Both. The orchestrator revision-cycle prompt for phase-scoped coders and the _build_agent_prompt revision feedback section. Mode commands serve as supplementary reference.

Q5_checkpoint_rule_sufficiency.question: Is the current checkpoint.md rule sufficient as the CLI reference?
Q5_checkpoint_rule_sufficiency.resolution: Yes for CLI reference (commands, filtering, workflows). Optionally add a brief 'When to Use' section at the top to bridge the gap between HOW (current rule) and WHEN/WHY (new hints).

Q6_issue_scope.question: What is the priority ordering of the 8 items in the issue?
Q6_issue_scope.resolution: Implement items 1-4 (agent mode commands, mission.md, orchestrator prompts, error recovery hints). Defer items 5-8 (slash command, handoff enrichment, revision summaries, egg-agent-context wrapper) to follow-up issues. Option A covers the highest-leverage changes.
